lines.text: Last night, my phone counted four thousand steps. I never left my bed. I know, because I filmed myself *sleeping.*
I'd been waking up exhausted for weeks. Sore legs. Dirt on my sheets. So I set up a camera, with my phone on the nightstand.
Phones count steps by feeling the bounce of someone walking. A phone sitting still counts *nothing.*
In the video, I'm asleep all night. I barely move.
But at 3:12, the phone on my nightstand is *gone.*
Forty minutes later, it's back. Same spot. No hand ever comes into frame. It's just gone, and then it isn't.
So I opened the step map. It draws every walk you take.
Four thousand two hundred steps. Starting at my nightstand. And the route is a *circle.*
Around my bed. Over and over. For forty minutes.
Something picked up my phone, and walked circles around me while I slept.
Then I looked down at the carpet.
There's a path worn into it. A perfect ring around my bed. That doesn't happen in one night. That takes *weeks.*
And now I know why I wake up so tired. Why my legs ache.
Some nights, it doesn't carry the phone.
